sents.d: Build tiered packages instead of guessing a day rate.
Most new videographers price by guessing an hourly rate, which punishes speed and undersells experience.
Instead, build 2–3 packages (e.g. Basic, Standard, Premium) defined by deliverables — number of final videos, turnaround time, and revision rounds — not hours worked.
Research what videographers with a similar portfolio charge in your area or niche before setting numbers, and price the middle package first since that's usually where most clients land.

scenes.heading: Raise prices on new clients first

sents.d: As your portfolio and demand grow, raise prices on new clients before raising them on existing ones, and communicate increases in advance rather than apologizing for them.

take: Price from research and packages, not a guessed hourly rate.
